items.name: Authority Matrix
items.summary: Governs how underwriting decision rights are assigned and escalated across the department, ensuring every risk is evaluated by someone with the demonstrated competence and formal mandate to accept it.

subs.title: Clear Authority Levels by Premium, Limit, and Line of Business
subs.description: Each underwriter's letter of authority specifies the maximum gross written premium, per-risk and aggregate limits, and the lines of business they may accept without escalation. Authority levels are reviewed at least annually and adjusted when an underwriter's role, performance, or portfolio results change. No risk may be accepted that exceeds any single dimension of the assigned authority, even if the others are within bounds.

subs.title: Documented Referral Triggers
subs.description: The matrix enumerates the specific conditions that force a referral upward, including premium or limit thresholds, hazardous classes, adverse loss history, non-standard terms, and out-of-appetite characteristics. Triggers are embedded in the underwriting workbench where feasible so they fire automatically rather than relying on underwriter recall, and the triggering condition is recorded in the file.

items.name: Binding Authority
items.summary: Controls who may commit the company to coverage and how those commitments are evidenced, protecting the carrier from unauthorized or undocumented exposure entering the book.

subs.title: Only Authorized Personnel Can Bind
subs.description: Coverage may be bound solely by individuals holding a current, written delegation of binding authority appropriate to the risk's premium, limit, and line of business. System access to issue binders is provisioned against the authority register, and any bind executed outside delegated authority is treated as an exception requiring immediate management review and ratification or rescission.

subs.title: Verbal Binders Documented Within 24 Hours
subs.description: When market conditions require a verbal commitment to a broker, the binding underwriter must issue a written binder confirming insured, coverage, limits, premium, effective date, and any subjectivities within 24 hours. The written confirmation is attached to the underwriting file, and unconfirmed verbal binders are escalated to underwriting management for resolution.

items.name: Referral Process
items.summary: Defines how risks outside an underwriter's authority move to the next decision level, so escalated accounts receive an informed, timely, and traceable decision rather than stalling in the pipeline.

subs.title: Referrals to Next Authority Level with Recommendation
subs.description: A referral package must go to the next level in the authority matrix and include the referring underwriter's analysis and an explicit recommendation to accept, decline, or modify terms. Forwarding a file without a position is not an acceptable referral; the referring underwriter remains accountable for the quality of the supporting analysis.

subs.title: Decision Documented Within 24 Hours
subs.description: The receiving authority records an accept, decline, or conditional decision in the underwriting file within 24 hours of receiving a complete referral, including the rationale and any conditions imposed. Referrals that cannot be decided in that window are flagged with the reason and a committed decision date communicated back to the broker-facing underwriter.

items.name: OFAC/Sanctions Screening
items.summary: Ensures the carrier does not provide coverage or pay funds to sanctioned parties by embedding sanctions checks into both new business and the life of the policy, protecting the company from regulatory penalties and reputational damage.

subs.title: All Insureds Screened Before Binding
subs.description: Named insureds, and where applicable beneficial owners and additional insureds, are screened against the current OFAC SDN list and other applicable sanctions lists before any binder or policy is issued. Potential matches are routed to Compliance for disposition, and binding is held until the match is cleared or the risk is declined.

subs.title: Ongoing Monitoring for Renewals
subs.description: The in-force book is rescreened as sanctions lists are updated, and every renewal passes through screening again before terms are released. A hit on an existing insured triggers immediate referral to Compliance, suspension of payments where required by law, and regulatory reporting in accordance with OFAC blocking and rejection rules.

items.name: Regulatory Compliance
items.summary: Keeps underwriting activity within the bounds of state insurance regulation by requiring that the forms, rates, and placement mechanisms used on every policy are properly filed, approved, or exempt before the company relies on them.

subs.title: Current Form Filings
subs.description: Only policy forms and endorsements that are filed and approved, or properly exempt, in the state of issue may be attached to a policy. Underwriting maintains form libraries in the policy administration system synchronized with the filing inventory, and withdrawn or superseded forms are deactivated so they cannot be issued in error.

subs.title: Rate Filings Approved Before Use
subs.description: Filed rates, rating plans, and rule manuals must have the required state approval or effective filing status before they are applied to new or renewal business. New rate levels are not loaded into rating engines ahead of their approved effective dates, and use-and-file jurisdictions follow the documented filing timeline.

subs.title: Surplus Lines Compliance
subs.description: Risks placed through the company's surplus lines paper must satisfy state eligibility and diligent search requirements, be transacted through a licensed surplus lines broker, and carry the required disclosures and stamping. Underwriters confirm the placement basis is documented in the file before binding non-admitted business.

items.name: Deviation Authority
items.summary: Controls how and when underwriters may depart from filed or technical rates, ensuring pricing flexibility is exercised within delegated limits and remains fully reconstructable for regulators and auditors.

subs.title: Deviation from Filed Rates per Authority Matrix
subs.description: Any credit, debit, or departure from the filed or technical rate must fall within the deviation bands granted to the underwriter in the authority matrix. Deviations beyond the assigned band require referral to the next authority level before the quote is released, and aggregate deviation usage is monitored at the portfolio level.

subs.title: Documentation Required
subs.description: Every deviation is supported by a written justification in the file that ties the adjustment to identifiable risk characteristics, competitive intelligence, or account considerations. Unsupported or boilerplate justifications are treated as documentation failures in quality review.

subs.title: Audit Trail Maintained
subs.description: The pricing system preserves a complete record of the technical rate, each deviation applied, the approver, and the timestamp, so the final premium can be reconstructed end to end. These records are retained per the corporate retention schedule and made available to Internal Audit, actuarial monitoring, and market conduct examiners.

items.name: Pricing Adequacy
items.summary: Ensures premiums charged across the portfolio are sufficient to cover expected losses and expenses by anchoring underwriting decisions to profitability targets, consistent tooling, and actuarial oversight of the largest exposures.

subs.title: Loss Ratio Targets by Line of Business
subs.description: Actuarial establishes target loss ratios for each line of business, and underwriters price individual accounts against those targets rather than against market rate alone. Performance versus target is reviewed in regular portfolio meetings, and persistent adverse variance triggers corrective pricing or appetite action.

subs.title: Mandatory Pricing Tool Usage
subs.description: All eligible accounts must be rated through the approved pricing tool so that the technical premium, selected premium, and rate adequacy ratio are captured consistently. Off-tool pricing is permitted only for documented system limitations and requires manager sign-off with the manual calculation attached to the file.

subs.title: Actuarial Review for Large Accounts
subs.description: Accounts exceeding the defined large-account threshold receive an actuarial review of exposure, loss development, and proposed pricing before the quote is released. The actuary's indicated price and the underwriter's selected price are both recorded, and material gaps between them must be explained and approved at the appropriate authority level.

items.name: Rating Standards
items.summary: Governs the mechanical application of approved rating plans so that every policy is priced accurately, defensibly, and at no less than the economic minimum the company will accept for putting its capital at risk.

subs.title: Filed Rates Applied Correctly
subs.description: Underwriters and rating systems must apply the filed base rates, classifications, territories, and rating factors exactly as approved, with classification decisions supported by the information in the file. Misclassification and manual overrides of system-calculated rates are tracked as rating errors and corrected through endorsement where discovered.

subs.title: Schedule Rating Documented
subs.description: Where schedule rating credits or debits are applied, the file must identify the specific risk characteristics supporting each modification and stay within the maximums allowed by the filed plan. Generic or unsupported schedule modifications are not permitted and are a standing focus of underwriting audit.

subs.title: Minimum Premium Enforced
subs.description: No policy may be issued below the minimum premium established for its line of business and program, regardless of credits or competitive pressure. Rating systems enforce the floor automatically, and any exception requires documented approval from underwriting management.

items.name: File Documentation
items.summary: Every bound account must carry a complete underwriting file containing the application, the risk analysis worksheet, the rationale for the selected pricing, and evidence of all required approvals, so that a reviewer can reconstruct why the risk was accepted on its terms without consulting the underwriter. Incomplete files are treated as quality defects subject to remediation timelines.

items.name: Peer Review
items.summary: Accounts generating more than $100,000 in premium must be reviewed by a second qualified underwriter before binding, with the reviewer assessing risk selection, terms, and pricing independently of the handling underwriter. The peer reviewer's concurrence or noted concerns are documented in the file, adding a structured second set of eyes on the accounts that carry the greatest potential to move portfolio results.

items.name: Underwriting Audit
items.summary: Establishes a layered inspection regime over underwriting quality, combining independent assurance with frequent management self-checks so that authority breaches, documentation gaps, and pricing errors are surfaced and corrected quickly.

subs.title: Annual Audit by Internal Audit
subs.description: Internal Audit performs an independent review of the underwriting function at least annually, testing adherence to authority limits, referral discipline, pricing standards, and file documentation. Findings are formally reported with agreed remediation owners and dates, and open items are tracked to closure through the audit committee process.

subs.title: Monthly 5% Sample Review by Underwriting Management
subs.description: Each month, underwriting management reviews a sample of at least 5% of bound accounts per underwriter against the quality checklist, scoring risk selection, rating accuracy, and documentation. Results feed individual coaching and authority decisions, and recurring deficiencies escalate to the chief underwriting officer.

items.name: Renewal Timeline
items.summary: Sets the working-backward calendar for every expiring policy so that renewal decisions are made deliberately, brokers and insureds receive terms with time to respond, and statutory notice obligations are never missed.

subs.title: Renewal Review 90 Days Out
subs.description: The handling underwriter begins the renewal evaluation no later than 90 days before expiration, refreshing exposure data, loss experience, and appetite fit, and ordering any updated inspections or financials needed. The intended renewal strategy, including restructure or non-renewal candidates, is identified at this point so downstream deadlines can be met.

subs.title: Quote to Broker 60 Days Out
subs.description: Renewal terms, conditions, and premium are released to the broker no later than 60 days before expiration for accounts the company intends to retain. Late quotes are tracked as a service metric, and accounts that cannot be quoted on time are escalated to management with the cause documented.

subs.title: Non-Renewal Notice per State Requirement
subs.description: When the company elects not to renew, conditional or final notice is issued within each state's statutory notice period and in the form the state prescribes, including required reasons where mandated. Notice generation is calendared against the longest applicable state requirement, and proof of mailing or delivery is retained in the file.

items.name: Retention Targets
items.summary: Directs the department's effort to keep profitable business on the books by setting measurable retention expectations and a disciplined response when desirable accounts leave.

subs.title: Retention Rate Targets by Segment
subs.description: Management sets policy-count and premium retention targets for each segment of the book, weighted toward the accounts the company most wants to keep. Actual retention is reported against target monthly, and segments running below plan receive a documented action plan covering pricing posture, service issues, or broker engagement.

subs.title: Win-Back Process for Lost Accounts
subs.description: Lost accounts that fit appetite are logged with the reason for loss, the competing carrier and terms where known, and a follow-up date ahead of the next renewal cycle. Targeted win-back outreach is coordinated with distribution, and lessons from loss reasons feed back into pricing and service improvements.

items.name: Prohibited Risks
items.summary: Draws the hard outer boundary of the underwriting appetite by codifying the classes and characteristics the company will not write, and ensures any breach of that boundary is a deliberate executive decision rather than an individual underwriter's call.

subs.title: No-Write List Maintained and Enforced
subs.description: A current list of prohibited classes, operations, geographies, and risk characteristics is owned by the chief underwriting officer's office, published to all underwriters and distribution partners, and coded into clearance and rating systems where possible. Submissions matching the list are declined at clearance, and any prohibited risk found on the in-force book is remediated at the next lawful opportunity.

subs.title: Exceptions Require CUO Approval with Documentation
subs.description: An account on the no-write list may be considered only with the chief underwriting officer's prior written approval, supported by a documented rationale covering the mitigating factors, terms, and pricing that justify the exception. Approved exceptions are logged centrally and reviewed periodically to confirm the conditions of approval still hold.

items.name: Risk Appetite Statement
items.summary: Provides the authoritative written expression of what business the company wants, keeping underwriters, executives, and distribution partners aligned on where capacity should be deployed and how that intent evolves over time.

subs.title: Documented Appetite by Line of Business, Geography, and Industry
subs.description: The appetite statement specifies, for each line of business, the target and acceptable classes, the geographies in which the company will deploy capacity, and the industries it favors, tolerates, or avoids. It is precise enough that an underwriter or broker can determine from the document alone whether a given account merits a submission.

subs.title: Updated Annually
subs.description: The statement is reviewed and reissued at least once a year as part of the planning cycle, incorporating portfolio performance, catastrophe accumulation, reinsurance structure, and market conditions. Material mid-year changes, such as a class restriction following adverse experience, are issued as formal amendments rather than informal guidance.

subs.title: Communicated to Distribution
subs.description: Current appetite is actively distributed to appointed agents and brokers through appetite guides, portal content, and producer meetings so that submission flow matches what the company wants to write. Changes are announced with effective dates, and submission quality metrics are used to confirm the message has landed.

items.name: Target Market Definition
items.summary: Translates the broad appetite statement into the specific account profiles the company is built to win, so underwriting and distribution effort concentrates where the value proposition is strongest.

subs.title: Target Classes Defined with Selection Criteria
subs.description: For each target market, the department documents the qualifying class codes and the selection criteria that distinguish a desirable account, such as size range, loss history, management quality, and exposure controls. These criteria are used at triage to prioritize submissions and in file reviews to test whether bound accounts genuinely fit the target profile.

subs.title: Hit Ratio Targets by Segment
subs.description: Quote-to-bind hit ratio expectations are set for each target segment and monitored against actuals to gauge competitiveness and submission quality. Hit ratios running well below target prompt review of pricing and terms, while ratios far above target are examined for signs of underpricing or adverse selection.

items.name: Declination Standards
items.summary: Governs how the company says no, ensuring declined business is handled with documented reasoning, prompt communication, and full compliance with notice obligations so brokers, insureds, and regulators are never left guessing.

subs.title: Declination Documented with Reason
subs.description: Every declined submission or renewal is recorded with the specific underwriting reason, such as out of appetite, adverse loss experience, or inadequate information, rather than a generic code. Documented reasons must be permissible under applicable unfair discrimination laws and are retained to support market conduct examinations.

subs.title: Decline Letter Within 24 Hours
subs.description: Written notice of declination is sent to the broker or applicant within 24 hours of the decision, stating that the company is declining and, where required or appropriate, the basis. Prompt notice preserves the broker's ability to place the risk elsewhere and reflects the service standard the company commits to its distribution partners.

subs.title: No Silent Non-Renewals
subs.description: An expiring policy may never simply lapse without an affirmative renewal or non-renewal decision communicated to the broker and insured. Every expiring account must show either issued renewal terms or a compliant non-renewal notice, and aging reports are monitored to catch policies approaching expiration without a recorded decision.

items.name: Minimum Submission Requirements
items.summary: A submission is not considered complete and ready for underwriting until it contains a signed application, five years of currently valued loss runs, the line-specific supplemental questionnaire, and a physical inspection where the class or exposure requires one. Incomplete submissions are returned to the broker with the missing items identified, and the service-standard clock starts only when the file is complete.

items.name: Submission Turnaround
items.summary: Establishes the service clock for new business handling so brokers receive predictable, competitive response times from first receipt through a bindable quote, protecting the company's position in the submission flow.

subs.title: Acknowledge Within 4 Hours
subs.description: Receipt of a submission is confirmed to the broker within 4 business hours, including the clearance result and the assigned underwriter. The acknowledgment also identifies any information missing against the minimum submission requirements so the broker can cure gaps immediately.

subs.title: Indication Within 48 Hours
subs.description: For complete, in-appetite submissions, the underwriter provides a non-binding pricing indication within 48 hours, giving the broker an early read on competitiveness. Out-of-appetite submissions are declined within the same window rather than held.

subs.title: Firm Quote Within 5 Business Days
subs.description: A formal, bindable quote with terms, conditions, and subjectivities is released within 5 business days of a complete submission for accounts the company elects to pursue. Quotes requiring referral or actuarial review remain subject to the same deadline, with delays escalated to management and communicated to the broker with a revised date.

items.name: Continuing Education
items.summary: Ensures the underwriting staff's technical capability keeps pace with the business they are authorized to write, linking ongoing learning directly to the authority each individual holds.

subs.title: 40 Hours of Continuing Education Annually
subs.description: Every underwriter completes at least 40 hours of qualifying continuing education each year, drawn from industry designations, regulatory courses, and approved internal programs. Completion is tracked centrally, counts toward state licensing CE where applicable, and shortfalls are addressed in the performance review cycle.

subs.title: Technical Training by Line of Business
subs.description: Underwriters receive structured technical curricula specific to the lines they handle, covering coverage forms, exposure analysis, rating plans, and emerging risks for that line. New lines of business or significant product changes trigger mandatory training before staff may underwrite the affected business.

subs.title: Authority Tied to Competency
subs.description: Increases in underwriting or binding authority are granted only on demonstrated competency, evidenced by training completion, audit scores, and file quality, rather than tenure alone. Sustained quality deficiencies can result in authority being reduced until remedial training and supervised file work restore the required standard.
